page_note: Page is overwhelmingly an ecclesial dialogue about the catechumen — specifically, the 'perfect catechumen' who is saved in a single body without further reincarnation. Two seam flags fire (i=7 'Ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ' + ekklektos, i=20 'Ⲧⲟⲧⲉ ⲡⲁⲭⲉ'). Significant editorial fatigue (+7.7 ecclesial drift in second half). The only substrate that survives is (a) the tail end of the previous chapter's soul-ascent teaching at segs 0-3 (ten angels raising up to the country of the Living Ones, rest, hope, works) and (b) the cosmological firmament-soul correspondence embedded inside the elect's question at segs 10-12 (soul fits to the firmaments that match its place of rest). Segs 23-31 describe the catechumen ideal — wife as stranger, house as lodging — pure institutional definition. Damage ratio 50%.
